entities.name: TBDMS-protected alcohol
observations: The substrate contains a benzylic/aryl-CH2-O-Si(CH3)2-tert-butyl ether, consistent with a TBDMS/TBS-protected alcohol.
The organic carbon framework, phosphate triester, and unsaturated groups are retained in the inferred transformation.

entities.name: Free benzylic alcohol
observations: The product contains the corresponding aryl/benzylic CH2OH group after cleavage of the O-Si bond.
The principal transformation is desilylation followed by protonation during workup.

entities.name: TBS ether deprotection
observations: The most plausible reaction class is fluoride-mediated TBDMS/TBS silyl-ether deprotection.
No exact empirical ORD record was retrieved; reagent recommendations are textbook-based rather than substrate-specific database matches.

entities.name: TBAF
observations: Tetrabutylammonium fluoride is the preferred reagent for cleaving the TBS ether.
Typical inferred conditions are approximately 1.1–1.5 equivalents in dry THF at 0 °C to room temperature, followed by aqueous or ammonium chloride workup.

entities.name: HF-pyridine
observations: HF-pyridine or related amine hydrofluoride is an alternative fluoride source for TBS deprotection, but requires stringent HF safety controls.

entities.name: Ammonium fluoride
observations: Ammonium fluoride is a milder alternative fluoride reagent, commonly used in methanol or aqueous alcohol for gradual TBS cleavage.
